newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SHAKE-OFF ATTACK ON COACH TO DRAW AT FIORENTINA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SHAKE-OFF ATTACK ON COACH TO DRAW AT FIORENTINA.

text.p: League leaders Juventus shook off an attack on their team coach by Florentine fans on Sunday to score a 1-1 draw against 10-man Fiorentina which kept them five points clear at the top of Serie A.

The Juventus players' coach was stoned on its way to the ground and although four windows were broken nobody was injured. Former champions AC Milan had two men sent off as they suffered their ninth defeat of the season.

Italy captain Paolo Maldini and French international Christophe Dugarry were both shown the red card as AC Milan slipped to a 1-0 defeat at struggling Perugia, which left them languishing in 11th place.
In Florence, Alessandro Del Piero steadied his Juventus team mates' nerves with a 16th-minute opener.
Fiorentina equalised through Anselmo Robbiati four minutes into the second half but settled for point after the dismissal of defender Daniele Carnasciali.

With second-placed Sampdoria needing an 88th-minute equaliser from Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic to cancel out Alain Boghossian's goal at Napoli, the top two positions in the table remained unchanged.
Juventus have 41 points from 21 matches, with Sampdoria five points adrift on 36.
Second-half goals from Youri Djorkaeff and Chilean Ivan Zamorano gave Inter a 2-0 win over Atalanta at the San Siro.
It was Atalanta's first defeat in 11 matches but the three points lifted Inter to third place on 34 points.
